question: In compression ultrasonography for deep vein thrombosis, the diagnostic criterion is loss of compressibility of the vein — a normal vein collapses completely under gentle transducer pressure, whereas a vein containing thrombus remains non-compressible because the clot resists deformation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The defining ultrasound sign of DVT is non-compressibility — the thrombus-filled segment does not collapse when gentle probe pressure is applied over the vein. This physical sign has high sensitivity and specificity for proximal DVT and is the cornerstone of the compression USG examination.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Loss of compressibility is the primary diagnostic criterion for DVT on ultrasound. A normal vein wall collapses to a thin line under probe pressure; thrombus prevents this. Doppler waveform changes (absent phasicity, loss of augmentation) are supplementary findings.
